aria: Animated recap of the Pacers' 114 to 101 home win over Washington: Andrew Nembhard's pull-up jumper with 9:04 left that capped a 14-0 fourth-quarter run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Pascal Siakam's 28 points on 12-of-12 free throws, the top scorers, how the Pacers won, and Friday's game with the Knicks.
notes: Box score from the Indiana Pacers' 114–101 home win over the Washington Wizards on Nov 11, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score, with game details from the AP (Mark Ambrogi, via theScore and infonews), Field Level Media, WISH-TV (via Yahoo Sports), Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker) and the Sportbusy play-by-play. All 114 Indiana points and all 101 Washington points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (55–50 Indiana at the half, matching the AP; 77–77 after three). Bench points (33–22) are worked out from the box score's starters; points in the paint (60–44) are from Field Level Media. Rebounds include team rebounds. Records and the Pacers' standing are from the site's standings.

Biggest leads: Washington's 8, at 41–33 midway through the second quarter (AP); Indiana's 16, at 100–84 and again at 112–96 in the fourth (Sportbusy play-by-play). Indiana closed the first half on a 22–9 run (AP), Washington closed the third on an 18–8 run to tie it 77–77 (AP), and Indiana opened the fourth with a 14–0 run (AP, Field Level Media). It was the Pacers' first home win of the season (Field Level Media, WISH-TV) and snapped a two-game skid (AP); Siakam's ninth 20-point game of the season is from WISH-TV. Aaron Nesmith left in the fourth with a sore right knee (Field Level Media).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Andrew Nembhard's pull-up jumper that capped the 14–0 run and gave Indiana a 91–77 lead (Field Level Media; the AP confirms the 14–0 run to 91–77). The 9:04 clock is from the Sportbusy play-by-play, where it is the basket that made it 91–77. It is drawn as the template's pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Indiana Pacers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Nembhard’s listed 6-foot-4 and 191 pounds (Basketball-Reference, RealGM), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-5.75 wingspan at the 2022 draft combine (Tankathon), in the Pacers' home white with No. 2 (Basketball-Reference, RealGM). He doesn't have an approved look yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
